doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Starting on drums, the Army, and drummer influences
summary: Roker began on marching drums at six, took up a drum set after being drafted in 1952, and names Kenny Clarke, Papa Jo Jones, Philly Joe Jones and Specs Wright as influences.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I started playing drums when I was about maybe six years old. And mostly military drums, marching band, stuff like that. And then I got drafted into the Army and that’s when I decided I wanted to play swing — a set of drums. So everybody that played drums was a big influence on me you know because when you don’t know anything, everything is exciting you know. But later on, after I learned about the drums, I fell in love with Kenny Clarke and Papa Jo Jones and Vernel Fournier, oh, so many people, you know Philly Joe Jones. But the guy that I listened to in my developing stages in Philadelphia was a drummer named Specs Wright. Because Philly Joe Jones had already gone by the time I started playing. I didn’t start playing until 1956. I got drafted in 1952 and I got out of the Army in 1955, so that’s when I started to play, practice and practice, and I’m still trying to learn how to play.
